questions.question: What does a 'Pairwise Difference Matrix' organize?
options: The differences between multiple pairs of numbers, laid out systematically to help spot a consistent pattern
questions.rationale: This matrix systematically organizes the differences across multiple number pairs, making it easier to visually spot a consistent underlying pattern.

questions.question: What does a 'Number Analogy Flowchart' provide?
options: A step-by-step decision path for identifying which numeric relationship (difference, ratio, square, etc.) applies
A synonym for the master pattern table
questions.rationale: This flowchart provides a systematic decision path for narrowing down which specific numeric relationship type applies to a given pair.

questions.question: What does a 'Letter Analogy Flowchart' provide, similarly?
options: The same flowchart as the number analogy one
A step-by-step decision path specifically for identifying which letter-based relationship (shift, mirror, etc.) applies
A flowchart only for word synonyms
questions.rationale: This flowchart provides the same systematic decision-path approach, but tailored specifically to identifying letter-based relationship types.

questions.question: What does a 'Word Analogy Flowchart' provide, in the same spirit?
options: A step-by-step decision path for identifying which word-based relationship (synonym, cause-effect, etc.) applies
The exact same flowchart as the letter analogy one
questions.rationale: This flowchart applies the same systematic approach specifically to word-based relationships, helping identify which category (synonym, antonym, cause-effect, etc.) fits.

questions.question: What does 'Analogy as Graph' model relationships as?
options: Nodes representing items connected by edges representing their relationships, similar to other structured reasoning graphs
Only numeric values with no connections
questions.rationale: This models analogy relationships as a graph, with items as nodes and their relationships as connecting edges — the same structural approach used in other reasoning topics.

questions.question: What is a 'Relationship Vector' in this context?
options: A representation of the specific transformation or relationship connecting one item to another, similar to a transformation vector in coding-decoding
questions.rationale: A relationship vector represents the specific transformation connecting two related items, paralleling the transformation vector concept from coding-decoding.

questions.question: What does 'Semantic Distance' measure?
options: The physical distance between two objects
How closely or distantly related two words' meanings are
The number of letters in a word
questions.rationale: Semantic distance measures how close or far apart two words' meanings are, which can help assess whether a candidate answer's relationship truly matches.

questions.question: What does 'Structural Analogy' emphasize, as opposed to purely semantic (meaning-based) analogy?
options: The abstract structural pattern of the relationship, which can apply even across superficially different domains
A relationship with no structure at all
questions.rationale: Structural analogy emphasizes the abstract pattern of the relationship itself, which can hold even when comparing items from very different domains, as long as the underlying structure matches.

questions.question: What does a 'Relationship Direction Matrix' organize?
options: The forward and reverse versions of common relationship types, to help avoid the direction trap
A synonym for the master pattern table
questions.rationale: This matrix organizes relationship types alongside both their forward and reverse directions, directly helping to avoid the direction trap covered earlier.

questions.question: What do 'Common Exam Relationships' likely consolidate?
options: A list of the most frequently tested relationship categories, to prioritize learning and recognition
questions.rationale: This section likely consolidates the most frequently tested relationship categories, helping prioritize which patterns are most valuable to recognize quickly.
